original_question: If a space X satisfies S_1(B_Ω, B_Ω), must every finite power of X satisfy S_1(B, B)? And if X satisfies S_fin(B_Ω, B_Ω), must every finite power of X satisfy S_1(B_Γ, B)?
target_in_paper: Section 8.2 (Finite powers), Problem 7(1)–(2), which is presented as the translation of the last two cases of Problem 6 in the Borel case.
correct_elements: The draft already captures the exact two implications asked in the paper’s official formulation of Problem 7: (1) whether S_1(B_Ω, B_Ω) implies that all finite powers satisfy S_1(B, B), and (2) whether S_fin(B_Ω, B_Ω) implies that all finite powers satisfy S_1(B_Γ, B). The finite-power aspect and the four selection properties are all correctly identified.
missing_details: The paper’s standing ambient scope is that, unless otherwise indicated, X is a set of reals (equivalently, one may think of a separable zero-dimensional metrizable space), not an arbitrary topological space.
The symbols B, B_Ω, and B_Γ should be defined: they are the families of countable Borel covers, countable Borel ω-covers, and countable Borel γ-covers of X, respectively.
The paper’s convention that a cover is nontrivial should be stated explicitly: U covers X, X = ⋃U, and X is not itself a member of U.

The meanings of ω-cover and γ-cover should be made explicit: every finite subset of X is contained in some member of an ω-cover; a γ-cover is infinite and each point of X belongs to all but finitely many members.
The operators S_1(U, V) and S_fin(U, V) should be defined explicitly in terms of selections from sequences of covers.
‘Every finite power of X’ should be quantified as X^n for each integer n ≥ 1.
To stay paper-faithful, the question should be presented as a two-part open problem from Section 8.2 rather than as an unspecified general preservation question.
refined_question: Let X be a set of reals. Let B, B_Ω, and B_Γ denote, respectively, the families of countable Borel covers, countable Borel ω-covers, and countable Borel γ-covers of X, where a cover U is nontrivial (X = ⋃U and X ∉ U), an ω-cover means that every finite F ⊆ X is contained in some U ∈ U, and a γ-cover means that U is infinite and each x ∈ X belongs to all but finitely many members of U. For collections U and V of covers, write S_1(U, V) if for every sequence (U_n)n∈N with each U_n ∈ U there exist U_n ∈ U_n such that {U_n : n ∈ N} ∈ V, and write S_fin(U, V) if for every such sequence there exist finite F_n ⊆ U_n such that ⋃n∈N F_n ∈ V. Must the following hold: (a) if X satisfies S_1(B_Ω, B_Ω), then X^n satisfies S_1(B, B) for every n ≥ 1; and (b) if X satisfies S_fin(B_Ω, B_Ω), then X^n satisfies S_1(B_Γ, B) for every n ≥ 1?
justification: The draft is essentially a near-verbatim restatement of the paper’s official Problem 7 in Section 8.2, page 189. To make it fully stand-alone, one must import the paper’s formal definitions of S_1 and S_fin from Section 2.1 (page 182), the standing convention that spaces are sets of reals unless otherwise stated from Section 2.3 (page 183), and the definitions of ω-covers, γ-covers, and the Borel families B, B_Ω, B_Γ from Section 3 (page 183). The nearby context in Section 8.2, especially Problem 6 and the sentence introducing Problem 7, shows that this is exactly the narrow finite-power preservation question the paper intends here, so the refinement keeps the two original subquestions without broadening them.
